source_span: An agent can destroy value in the human facing interface while creating more activity underneath it... Anything earning excess returns from friction, complexity or inertia should get nervous.
source_chain: Agents shift activity from the human-facing interface to the rails underneath (booking, payment, custody, settlement) therefore any business earning excess returns from friction, complexity or inertia is structurally exposed therefore Goldman's Miller (17349) shorts Consumer Inertia (GSXUSWCH) because agents compress the switching costs that used to be booked as a moat, and the basket (Jeter, 17513) falls -2.58% led by PLNT/NYT/SCHW/ALL/INTU. Invalidation: JPMorgan's O'Dwyer (17527) disputes the bank-specific read as a positioning unwind rather than a re-rating and fades the move (favoring MS/PNC/FITB), and the desk's own house view (17527) states it turns bearish only on 'signs the Consumer and economy are breaking or that the AI theme has ended, initiated by a capex cut' — otherwise the short thesis holds.
pulse_chain: Agents move activity off human-facing screens onto the plumbing underneath therefore any business earning a return from friction, complexity or inertia is exposed while booking, payments and settlement gain volume therefore Goldman's Miller shorts Consumer Inertia on that logic therefore the basket falls with PLNT/NYT/SCHW/ALL/INTU named worst, contested by JPMorgan's O'Dwyer (positioning unwind, not a re-rating, fades the move favoring MS/PNC/FITB) with Goldman's own financials desk in the middle (uncertainty discount, buyers' strike, no sector defense). Invalidation: whether inertia names keep falling once compute stops rallying, with JPMorgan turning bearish only on a consumer break or an AI capex cut.
why: Every step, the attribution of the short thesis to Goldman's Miller versus the dispute to JPMorgan's O'Dwyer, the supporting data (basket -2.58%, the five named laggards), and the invalidation condition are all reproduced with the same direction and the invalidation line is a near-verbatim match to JPM's own stated bearish trigger.
